_README: Label id -> structure name for the body-surface volume built from the Visible Human male's OWN CT (three blocks: torso, legs, feet) by scripts/cryo/vhm_whole_body_skin.py: HU > -300 silhouette per slice, opened, holes filled, largest connected body kept, then a 2 mm dilation margin. Replaces the earlier torso-only version built from his colour cryosections (scripts/cryo/skin_from_cryo.py), which needs a DU-blocked re-stream and never covered the legs.
source: U.S. National Library of Medicine, The Visible Human Project (public domain), male frozen CT, IDC series 5d409385-d3e7-48a9-ae50-150b39e834da (torso), 145c2668-7d2f-4d7e-b1c7-2cf2462bef60 (legs), 94755b62-0f88-4aa8-82ec-2d6d5cb8dbc7 (feet); see docs/GEOMETRY_SOURCES.md 'Stage 2'.

body_surface.note: Whole-body silhouette at 1 mm covering head to toes. The torso<->legs and legs<->feet block shifts are fitted directly against the DU-STL bone/muscle vertices already shipped in vhm_both (not the raw image-correlation shifts recorded when the CT blocks were first registered), because those left up to 42% of tarsal/phalanx vertices and 15-17% of thigh/calf muscle vertices outside the silhouette. A 2 mm dilation margin brings mean vertex containment failure across all 130 vhm_both structures to 0.03% (worst case fibularis_longus_r, 1.8%).
